bulk.title: Bulk edit
bulk.title.hint: applies to every entry in the list below
bulk.hintBool: Yes/No stat: use "Set to" with true or false.
bulk.hintMultiply: 150 = +50%, 50 = half. Based on each entry's original value.
bulk.hintAdd: Adds to each entry's original value (use a negative number to subtract).
bulk.hintReset: Removes this stat's edit from every listed entry.
bulk.hintSet: Sets the same value on every listed entry.
bulk.invalid: Bulk edit: enter a valid value.
bulk.done: Bulk edit: {0} changed on {1} of {2} listed. Review under Changes; Discard undoes everything unsaved.

detail.pickUnit: Pick a unit on the left
detail.pickWeapon: Pick a weapon on the left
detail.pickHint: Change any stat, then press Save. Only the stats you change are written; the game's own files are never modified.
detail.noChanged: No changed stats on this entry.
detail.catalogOriginals: originals from BattleSector Tools until the game files are read

paint.intro: Recolour a faction everywhere it appears — battle, army management and menus, your army and enemies alike. Pick a faction, then a colour for its main armour (Primary) and trim (Secondary). Factions left at their default colours are not touched.
paint.reset.tip: Back to this faction's default colours.
paint.previewHint: Approximate: the same recolour code the game uses, run on this faction's unit portraits. In battle it also runs on the 3D model textures, so the models differ a little.
paint.tuneHint: If parts of the model don't change colour, raise Colour match width. If metal or skin changes too, raise Ignore greys.
paint.inGame1: Every unit model of a faction with a custom scheme is repainted automatically — in battle (both sides), army management and menus.
paint.inGame2: Save here while the game runs — the colours update within about a second.
paint.inGame3: In game, the "Army Painter" button (top-right) or {0} opens a small window to tweak and Apply.
paint.inGame4: Enemies of the same faction are painted too. Nothing in the game files is changed; set a faction back to default colours to restore its stock paint.
paint.noPortraits: No portraits bundled for this faction.
paint.enable.hint: Opt-in. Painting only starts when this is on and at least one faction has a custom colour or scheme. Editing only unit stats never turns it on.
paint.enable.off: Off: every faction keeps the game's own paint, and Warpstorm does no paint work.
paint.enable.idle: On, but every faction is still at its default colour, so nothing will be repainted yet.
paint.enable.on: On: {0} faction(s) will be repainted in game.
paint.importPack.tip: Install a curated scheme (.zip with scheme.json and portraits), e.g. Salamanders. It is copied to BepInEx/config/warpstorm/schemes.
paint.imported: Installed scheme '{0}' for {1}. Pick it under Scheme, then Save.
paint.importFailed: Could not import the scheme pack: {0}
paint.packNote: Curated: models use the pack's recipe, portraits use its hand-made art.
paint.noPacks: No scheme packs for this faction yet — use custom colours, or Import scheme pack….

settings.folderHint: The folder that contains "{0}". Found automatically when this tool runs from the mod folder.
settings.startMenuHint: Optional: add "Warpstorm Configurator" to the Start menu so you don't have to find it in the game folder again. It points at this copy of the program.
settings.shortcutPresent: Shortcut present in the Start menu.
setting.warpstorm.Enabled.hint: Master switch. Also toggled live in game with the toggle key.
setting.warpstorm.ShowStatus: Show the Warpstorm box in game
setting.warpstorm.ShowStatus.hint: Small top-left box with status, Toggle / Reload buttons and Open Configurator.
setting.armypainter.ToggleKey: Open the in-game Army Painter window
setting.armypainter.ShowButton: Show the Army Painter button in game
setting.armypainter.Enabled.hint: Off by default. While off, the plugin does no paint work at all. Turn it on, then change a faction colour or pick a scheme and Save.
setting.armypainter.AutoApply.hint: Paint every unit model of a faction with a custom scheme as soon as it appears (battle, army management, menus).
setting.armypainter.ApproxPortraits.hint: Hue-shifts the 2D unit portraits of factions with a custom scheme. Quality is rough, so it is off by default.
setting.armypainter.HueWindow.hint: How far from the detected paint colour a pixel may be and still be repainted. Higher = more of the model changes.
setting.armypainter.SatThreshold.hint: Pixels less saturated than this (metal, grime, bone) are left alone.
setting.armypainter.BlendFeather.hint: Soft blend at the edge of the colour match.
setting.armypainter.DiagMode.hint: Writes detailed [ArmyPainter] DIAG lines to BepInEx/LogOutput.log. Turn on only when reporting a bug.
help.headline: Edit → Save → play
help.step1: Pick a unit or weapon, change any stat. Leave a box empty to keep the game's value.
help.step2: Army Painter (opt-in): switch "Army Painter in game" on, then pick your faction and new colours.
help.step3: Press Save (Ctrl+S). If the game is running it reloads automatically and this window confirms it; otherwise changes apply the next time you start the game.
help.keys: In game: {0} turns stat edits on/off, {1} reloads, {2} opens Army Painter. The small Warpstorm box (top-left) has the same buttons, plus "Open Configurator".
help.whereBody: It ships inside the mod at  <game folder>\BepInEx\plugins\Warpstorm\Warpstorm.Configurator.exe.
help.whereEasier: Easier ways to open it: the "Open Configurator" button in the in-game Warpstorm box; Vortex → Dashboard → Tools → Warpstorm Configurator; or Settings → Add to Start menu.
help.good1: Only the stats you change are written. The game's own files are never modified, so it stacks with other mods.
help.good2: Weapon edits apply to every unit that carries that weapon (see "Used by").
help.good3: Single-player only. Changing stats in multiplayer is cheating — don't.
help.good4: If something does not apply: Settings → Files → Game log, and look for [Warpstorm] / [ArmyPainter] lines.
help.aboutLine: Warpstorm Configurator {0} · crystal-mods · unit data from BattleSector Tools
help.disclaimer: Fan-made. Not affiliated with Black Lab Games or Games Workshop.
bake.title: Bake textures
bake.hint: Paints your factions' model textures here, ahead of time, so the game only has to load them — painting in game becomes near-instant. Runs automatically after Save; takes about a minute per faction. Textures the bake can't reach are still painted in game (once, then cached).
bake.now.tip: Saves, then paints every model texture of factions with a custom scheme into BepInEx/cache/warpstorm/paint.
bake.clear.tip: Deletes BepInEx/cache/warpstorm/paint. The game falls back to painting live.
bake.noBundle: {0}: no faction bundle found; painted in game instead.
bake.done: Bake finished: {0} painted, {1} already up to date, {2} failed ({3} s). The game loads them instantly.
bake.cancelled: Bake cancelled — finished textures are kept.
bake.nothing: No faction has a custom scheme yet — nothing to bake.
setting.armypainter.MaxTextureSize.hint: The game's textures are 4096 px. 2048 looks nearly identical and needs a quarter of the memory and disk; 1024 is lighter still.
creator.open.tip: Design a paint scheme for any faction with a live preview, then use it or share it as a .zip.
creator.editCopy.tip: Open the selected scheme (or a fresh one) in the Scheme Creator.
creator.title: Paint your own army
creator.step1.hint: Pick the game faction whose models you repaint, and name your scheme (e.g. "Ultramarines → Iron Lords").
creator.name: Scheme name
creator.author: Author
creator.step2.hint: Each rule turns one colour of the original paint into a new colour. Select a rule, then click a colour on an ORIGINAL portrait on the right to pick it. Width widens the matched colour range; Brightness and Saturation fine-tune the result.
creator.sourceTip: Colour this rule picks up from the original paint
creator.eyedropper.tip: Make this the rule that the next click on an original portrait sets.
creator.step3.hint: Replaces the chapter symbol on the 3D armour. Use a built-in badge or your own PNG: a white shape on a transparent background, square, ideally 512 px.
creator.badgeUnavailable: {0} paints its chapter symbol straight into the armour texture, so a badge swap isn't available for it (it is for Ultramarines-based schemes).
creator.step4.hint: Save installs the scheme and selects it for the faction (then press Save at the top to apply it in game). Export creates a .zip others can install with Import scheme pack….
creator.save.tip: Installs into BepInEx/config/warpstorm/schemes and selects it for the faction.
creator.previewHint: Left: original — click it to pick a colour for the selected rule. Right: your scheme. The game applies exactly the same rules to the models and portraits.
creator.loadModels: Load model textures from the game
creator.loadModels.tip: Reads a few of this faction's model textures from the game files (read-only) for a 3D preview.
creator.loadingModels: Reading model textures from the game files…
creator.loadedModels: Loaded {0} model texture(s) for the preview.
creator.pickTip: Click to pick this colour for the selected rule
creator.picked: Picked hue {0}°, saturation {1}%, brightness {2}% for rule {3}.
creator.saved: Saved scheme '{0}' and selected it for {1}. Press Save at the top to apply it in game.
help.tut1: Army Painter → Create your own scheme… (or select a scheme and click Edit a copy).
help.tut2: Pick the base faction — the game faction whose models get repainted — and give the scheme a name.
help.tut3: Rule 1 is the main armour colour. Click Pick colour, then click the armour on an original portrait; choose the new colour in the colour box.
help.tut4: Rule 2 catches highlights. Add rules for trim or other parts; raise Colour match width if parts stay unchanged, raise Ignore greys if metal or skin change too.
help.tut5: Load model textures from the game to check the 3D result; tune Brightness / Saturation until it looks right.
help.tut6: Optional: choose a chapter badge (white PNG on transparent) for Ultramarines-based schemes.
help.tut7: Save & use, then Save at the top. The configurator bakes the textures; start or return to the game. Export .zip… to share it.
